skill.name: context-receipts
skill.description: Emit privacy-safe receipts for context selection, tool loading, retrieval, compaction, pruning, delegation, and boundary handoffs.
skill.summary: Create privacy-safe audit receipts for agent context boundaries.
skill.author: caioribeiroclw-pixel

security_audit.summary: No confirmed malicious behavior was found in the scanned files. The README path findings are fixed documentation links or fixture commands, and the SKILL.md findings are Markdown formatting. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or unauthorized network behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: - an `audit_gap` field when the receipt proves routing but not semantic correctness.
- which validation outcome applied, such as `accepted`, `blocked_by_rai`, `blocked_by_xpia`, `schema
For subagents that should inherit MCP through `ToolSearch`, distinguish policy, declaration, and run
- was the `tools:` declaration wildcard, explicit include, or exclusion style?
- was `ToolSearch` declared and was it actually exposed in the subagent tool surface?
For `/usage`, `/context`, `/doctor`, or other context-budget breakdowns, map each displayed category
1. **Index-only startup:** did the session load a compact tool/server index instead of all full sche
4. **Call:** which server/tool id was invoked, with argument/result redaction status and success/err
5. **Boundary:** if a manager subagent or child agent was used, did raw child output return to the p
- what the agent must stop on if a required id is missing;
- did the parent/orchestrator intend to expose MCP or exclude it for this subagent?
- did MCP servers/tool definitions stay deferred, or did the channel collapse to zero?
- did the summary call succeed, fail, or timeout;
- did the harness commit a context swap or preserve the original context;
- did stale system reminders/tool results replay as fresh state;

content.value_statement: Context workflows can hide what entered or left an agent window. This skill defines privacy-safe receipts that show routing, deferral, hydration, pruning, and audit gaps.
actual_capabilities: Defines receipt fields for Tool Search, MCP hydration, and runtime tool-surface changes.
Shows privacy defaults for excluding prompts, schemas, results, transcripts, secrets, and customer names.
Provides event examples for context attention, pruning, compaction, and delegation workflows.
Lists checks for subagent MCP policy, ToolSearch propagation, usage attribution, and manager handoffs.
Uses audit_gap fields to separate boundary evidence from semantic correctness.
Supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows through markdown instructions.
limitations: It does not run validators or parse receipt files by itself.
It cannot prove a tool or retrieved document was semantically correct.
It depends on the host agent or harness to emit the requested receipt events.
The README points to external examples that are not included in this skill package.

use_cases.title: Audit MCP Tool Loading
use_cases.description: Check whether tool schemas were deferred, hydrated, or suppressed without exposing raw schema text.

use_cases.title: Review Retrieval Attention
use_cases.description: Confirm selected context ids were delivered, acknowledged, and cited before edits or tool calls.

use_cases.title: Document Compaction Safety
use_cases.description: Record what pruning or compaction changed, protected, backed up, or rolled back.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Tool Search Receipt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for one MCP Tool Search workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context-receipts for this Tool Search workflow. Report only counts, hashed ids, redaction flags, token buckets, and audit_gap.

prompt_templates.title: Context Attention Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for retrieved context before edits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context-receipts to verify retrieved context. Show selected ids, delivered ids, acknowledged ids, cited ids, missing stop rule, and audit_gap.

prompt_templates.title: Compaction Transaction Receipt
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for pruning, compaction, or rollback behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context-receipts for this pruning or compaction run. Include trigger, before and after buckets, protected summaries, rollback state, and audit_gap.

prompt_templates.title: Boundary Audit Across Agents
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit for manager and subagent workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context-receipts across manager and subagent steps. Compare delegated task category, child output buckets, returned summary bounds, raw content flags, and audit_gap.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether Tool Search reduced context load for an MCP workflow.
output: Receipt confirms an index-only startup with no full schemas loaded.
One tool definition was hydrated after routing, and suppressed definitions stayed deferred.
Audit gap states this does not prove the tool choice was optimal.

output_examples.input: A maintainer reviews a failed compaction attempt.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a concise receipt showing the failed summary status, rollback preservation, restored registries, and no copied raw transcript text.

output_examples.input: A team checks whether a subagent returned too much context.
output: The receipt records the delegated task category and child output size bucket.
It states whether raw child output returned to the parent context.
It names the remaining audit gap for reviewer follow-up.

best_practices: Use hashed ids, counts, buckets, and booleans instead of raw prompts or outputs.
Always include audit_gap so reviewers understand what the receipt cannot prove.
Record before and after context-budget buckets for hydration, pruning, and compaction events.
anti_patterns: Do not copy raw prompts, schemas, tool arguments, tool results, secrets, or customer text into receipts.
Do not claim a tool choice was correct only because a receipt exists.
Do not use vague statements such as Tool Search enabled without boundary evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. SKILL.md is markdown guidance. The README shows optional fixture commands for examples outside the skill package.

faq.question: What data should receipts include?
faq.answer: Use stable ids, hashes, counts, token buckets, booleans, outcome codes, and audit_gap fields.

faq.question: Can it replace security logging?
faq.answer: No. It complements logging by documenting context boundaries without exposing private content.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is markdown guidance that can be applied in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How should private context be handled?
faq.answer: Keep raw prompts, schemas, tool outputs, transcripts, secrets, and customer text out of receipts.

faq.question: What is audit_gap?
faq.answer: It is a short statement of what the receipt proves and what it does not prove.
